competency_fulfillment.rationale: Recomputed all 10 mL answer keys by round-half-up and every one matches: notably seed 43's 5 mL now keys to 10 (was wrongly 0 in the prior review round), resolving the midpoint bug that previously made this node's own answer key internally inconsistent.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The lc text names both 'liters and/or milliliters', yet all 10 samples in this batch are exclusively milliliters (5 to 64); no liter-scale item, which would involve a larger container, appears anywhere here.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: 'An object's capacity measures 46 mL. About how many mL is that, rounded to the nearest 10?' is two short plain sentences with a single arithmetic step, well within grade-3 quarter-2 reading and reasoning demand.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The batch mixes round-down cases (41, 64, 32), round-up-from-below-half cases (46, 9), a value already at a tens multiple (10), and two genuine midpoints (5, 35) that both now round up consistently, covering the full behavior space of the round-half-up rule.

competency_alignment.rationale: The item structure mirrors the sibling mass node with only the unit swapped to mL, and every question supplies an exact known volume to round rather than asking the student to judge an unmeasured container's capacity by benchmark comparison as 'estimate capacity' implies.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The mL magnitudes (5 through 64) describe a small container-sized volume, an appropriately modest two-digit scale for a grade-3 quarter-2 introduction to capacity estimation.
